Get or set global default plot styles

Source: R/plot-options.R
plot_options.Rd

Configure package-wide defaults for plot.cgraph()'s node_style, edge_style, label_style, and title_style arguments, so every plot picks them up without repeating the same style lists at every call site. Arguments passed directly to plot() still take precedence over these global defaults.

Usage

plot_options(...)

Arguments

...

Named values to update options with (merged into the existing options via utils::modifyList(), so a partial style list only overrides the fields it mentions), or unnamed option names to retrieve. Multiple unnamed arguments drill down through nested options. Called with no arguments, returns all current plot options. Querying a non-existent option raises an error.

Value

When setting, the previous values for the updated options, invisibly. When getting, the requested options.

Details

Fields, matching the corresponding plot.cgraph() argument:

  • node_style: fill, col, lwd, padding (mm), size (multiplier), radius (mm, fixed override), shape ("circle", "square", "ellipse", or "rect"), linestyle (e.g. "dashed")

  • edge_style: col, lwd, lty, fill (arrowhead fill), arrow_size (mm), circle_size (mm), gap (mm), curvature (signed fraction of edge length; unset by default, so parallel edges between the same node pair fan out automatically - see plot.cgraph()), and the edge label fields label_col, label_fontsize, label_fontface, label_fontfamily, label_shift, label_distance (mm), label_rotation (degrees)

  • label_style: col, fontsize, fontface, fontfamily, cex

  • title_style: same fields as label_style

See plot.cgraph() for the full description of each field. Per-type (edge_style$directed, ...) and per-node/per-edge (by_node, by_edge, label_style$by_node) overrides stay plot()-call arguments only - they are not part of these global defaults.

See also

plot.cgraph() for per-plot style arguments and per-node/edge overrides, plot_default_options() to inspect or reset to the built-in defaults.

Other plotting: cgraph_layout(), plot.cgraph(), plot_default_options()

Examples

# Query all current plot options
plot_options()
#> $node_style
#> $node_style$fill
#> [1] "white"
#> 
#> $node_style$col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $node_style$lwd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $node_style$padding
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $node_style$size
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $node_style$shape
#> [1] "circle"
#> 
#> 
#> $edge_style
#> $edge_style$col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $edge_style$lwd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $edge_style$arrow_size
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $edge_style$circle_size
#> [1] 1.5
#> 
#> $edge_style$gap
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $edge_style$label_col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $edge_style$label_fontsize
#> [1] 9
#> 
#> $edge_style$label_shift
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> 
#> $label_style
#> $label_style$col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $label_style$fontsize
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> 
#> $title_style
#> $title_style$col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $title_style$fontsize
#> [1] 14
#> 
#> $title_style$fontface
#> [1] "bold"
#> 
#> 

# Query one option
plot_options("node_style")
#> $fill
#> [1] "white"
#> 
#> $col
#> [1] "black"
#> 
#> $lwd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $padding
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $size
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $shape
#> [1] "circle"
#> 

# Drill into a nested option
plot_options("node_style", "fill")
#> [1] "white"

# Set a global default node fill
plot_options(node_style = list(fill = "lightblue"))

# Set multiple defaults at once
plot_options(
  node_style = list(fill = "lightblue", col = "navy"),
  edge_style = list(col = "gray40", lwd = 1.5)
)

# Reset to defaults
plot_options(plot_default_options())
